A cat(1) clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration.

## Key Features ### Syntax highlighting `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. ### Git integration `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. ### Show non-printable characters You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. ### Automatic paging By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. #### File concatenation Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. ## How to use Display a single file on the terminal: ```bash bat README.md ``` Display multiple files at once: ```bash bat src/*.rs ``` Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: ```bash curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat ``` Read from stdin, specify the language explicitly: ```bash yaml2json .travis.yml | json_pp | bat -l json ``` Show and highlight non-printable characters: ```bash bat -A /etc/hosts ``` Use it as a `cat` replacement: ```bash bat > note.md # quickly create a new file bat header.md content.md footer.md > document.md bat -n main.rs # show line numbers (only) bat f - g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. ``` ### Integration with other tools #### `fzf` You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: ```bash fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" ``` #### `find` or `fd` Preview all search results with `bat`: ```bash find … -exec bat {} + fd … -X bat ``` #### `ripgrep` With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: ```bash batgrep needle src/ ``` #### `tail -f` `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: ```bash tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log ``` #### `git` Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: ```bash git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs ``` #### `git diff` Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: ```bash batdiff() { git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff } ``` #### `xclip` Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: ```bash bat main.cpp | xclip ``` `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. #### `man` `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: ```bash export MANPAGER="bat -plman" man 2 select ``` #### Highlighting `--help` messages You can use `bat` to colorize help text: ```bash cp --help | bat -plhelp ``` Or use a wrapper: ```bash alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' help() { "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp } ``` ## Installation Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. `bat` is also available through various package managers: - Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt install bat` - Alpine: `apk add bat` - Arch: `pacman -S bat` - Fedora: `dnf install bat` - Gentoo: `emerge sys-apps/bat` - FreeBSD: `pkg install bat` - OpenBSD: `pkg_add bat` - Nix: `nix-env -i bat` - openSUSE: `zypper install bat` - macOS (Homebrew): `brew install bat` - macOS (MacPorts): `port install bat` - Windows (WinGet): `winget install sharkdp.bat` - Windows (Chocolatey): `choco install bat` - Windows (Scoop): `scoop install bat` ## Customization ### Highlighting theme Use `bat --list-themes` to get a list of all available themes for syntax highlighting. To select a theme, use the `--theme` option: ```bash bat --theme=TwoDark myfile.txt ``` Or set the `BAT_THEME` environment variable: ```bash export BAT_THEME="TwoDark" ``` `bat` automatically picks a fitting theme depending on your terminal's background color. You can use the `--theme-dark` / `--theme-light` options or the `BAT_THEME_DARK` / `BAT_THEME_LIGHT` environment variables to customize the themes used. ### Output style Use the `--style` option to control the appearance of `bat`'s output: ```bash bat --style=numbers,changes myfile.txt ``` Set the `BAT_STYLE` environment variable to make these changes permanent. ### Decorations By default, `bat` only shows decorations when outputting to an interactive terminal. Control this with the `--decorations` option: ```bash bat --decorations=always myfile.txt # always show decorations bat --decorations=never myfile.txt # never show decorations ``` ### Using a different pager `bat` uses the pager specified in the `PAGER` environment variable. If not set, `less` is used by default. You can also use bat's built-in pager with `--pager=builtin`. To use a different pager: ```bash export BAT_PAGER="less -RF" ``` ### Configuration file `bat` can be customized with a configuration file. To get the default path: ```bash bat --config-file ``` Generate a default configuration file: ```bash bat --generate-config-file ``` The configuration file is a simple list of command line arguments. Example: ```bash # Set the theme --theme="TwoDark" # Show line numbers, Git modifications and file header --style="numbers,changes,header" # Use C++ syntax for Arduino .ino files --map-syntax "*.ino:C++" ``` ## Command-line options For a full list of options, run: ```bash bat --help ``` ## Project goals `bat` tries to achieve the following goals: - Provide beautiful, advanced syntax highlighting - Integrate with Git to show file modifications - Be a drop-in replacement for (POSIX) `cat` - Offer a user-friendly command-line interface ## License Copyright (c) 2018-2025 bat-developers `bat` is made available under the terms of either the MIT License or the Apache License 2.0, at your option. 5. Non-printable notation.
6. Binary detection.
7. Wrapping.
8. Highlight-line.
9. Multiple -r ranges.
10. Git changes.

Let me test each. First, tab width default.

# Requires https://github.com/scop/bash-completion

# Macs have bash3 for which the bash-completion package doesn't include
# _init_completion. This is a minimal version of that function.
__bat_init_completion()
{
	COMPREPLY=()
	_get_comp_words_by_ref "$@" cur prev words cword
}

__bat_escape_completions()
{
	# Do not escape if completing a quoted value.
	[[ $cur == [\"\']* ]] && return 0
	if ((
		BASH_VERSINFO[0] > 5 || \
		BASH_VERSINFO[0] == 5 && BASH_VERSINFO[1] >= 3
	)); then
		# bash >= 5.3 has "compopt -o fullquote", which exactly does
		# what this function tries to do.
		compopt -o fullquote
	elif ((
		BASH_VERSINFO[0] > 4 || \
		BASH_VERSINFO[0] == 4 && BASH_VERSINFO[1] > 0
	)); then
		# printf -v to an array index is available in bash >= 4.1.
		# Use it if available, as -o filenames is semantically
		# incorrect if we are not actually completing filenames, and it
		# has side effects (e.g. adds trailing slash to candidates
		# matching present dirs).
		local i
		for i in ${!COMPREPLY[*]}; do
			printf -v "COMPREPLY[i]" %q "${COMPREPLY[i]}"
		done

		# We can use "compopt -o noquote" available in bash >= 4.3 to
		# prevent further quoting by the shell, which would be
		# unexpectedly applied when a quoted result matches a filename.

			BASH_VERSINFO[0] > 4 || \
			BASH_VERSINFO[0] == 4 && BASH_VERSINFO[1] >= 3
		)); then
			compopt -o noquote
		fi
	else
		compopt -o filenames
	fi
}

# Fish Shell Completions
# Copy or symlink to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fish/completions/bat.fish
# ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME is usually set to ~/.config)

# `bat` is `batcat` on Debian and Ubuntu
set bat bat

# Helper functions:

function __bat_complete_files -a token
    # Cheat to complete files by calling `complete -C` on a fake command name,
    # like `__fish_complete_directories` does.
    set -l fake_command aaabccccdeeeeefffffffffgghhhhhhiiiii
    complete -C"$fake_command $token"
end

function __bat_complete_one_language -a comp
    command $bat --list-languages | string split -f1 : | string match -e "$comp"
end

function __bat_complete_list_languages
    for spec in (command $bat --list-languages)
        set -l name (string split -f1 : $spec)
        for ext in (string split -f2 : $spec | string split ,)
            test -n "$ext"; or continue
            string match -rq '[/*]' $ext; and continue
            printf "%s\t%s\n" $ext $name
        end
        printf "%s\t\n" $name
    end
end

function __bat_complete_map_syntax
    set -l token (commandline -ct)

    if string match -qr '(?<glob>.+):(?<syntax>.*)' -- $token
        # If token ends with a colon, complete with the list of language names.
        set -f comps $glob:(__bat_complete_one_language $syntax)
    else if string match -qr '\*' -- $token
        # If token contains a globbing character (`*`), complete only possible
        # globs in the current directory
        set -f comps (__bat_complete_files $token | string match -er '[*]'):
    else
        # Complete files (and globs).
        set -f comps (__bat_complete_files $token | string match -erv '/$'):
    end

    if set -q comps[1]
        printf "%s\t\n" $comps
    end
end

function __bat_cache_subcommand
    __fish_seen_subcommand_from cache
end

# Returns true if no exclusive arguments seen.
function __bat_no_excl_args
    not __bat_cache_subcommand; and not __fish_seen_argument \
        -s h -l help \

- flag: "--show-all"

{"command": "cd /workspace; cat > /tmp/ext1.py <<'PY'
import subprocess,re
themes=[l.strip() for l in open('assets/themes.txt') if l.strip()]
def segs(args):
    p=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True)
    out=p.stdout.decode('utf8','replace')
    parts=re.split(r'(\x1b\[[0-9;]*m)',out)
    r=[];cur=''
    for x in parts:
        if x.startswith('\x1b['): cur=x[2:-1]
        elif x: r.append((cur,x))
    return r
D='\u2500'
print("THEME | frame | fg | marker~ | marker+ | marker- | hdr_lab | hdr_name | empty/binary")
for t in themes:
    a=segs(['./executable','--color=always','--decorations=always','--theme='+t,'/tmp/pt.txt'])
    frame=None
    for s,x in a:
        if D in x and len(x)>10 and x.count(D)>5: frame=s; break
    fg=[s for s,x in a if x.strip()=='hello']
    # marker colors
    b=segs(['./executable','--color=always','--decorations=always','--theme='+t,'-d','--diff-context=0','/tmp/gt/df.txt'])
    til=[s for s,x in b if x.strip()=='~']
    plus=[s for s,x in b if x.strip() in ('+','-')]
    print(t,'|',frame,'|',fg[0] if fg else None,'|',til[0] if til else None,'|',plus[:2])
PY
python3 /tmp/ext1.py"}

import subprocess,re,json,os

    p=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,env=e)
    out=p.stdout.decode('utf8','replace')
    parts=re.split(r'(\x1b\[[0-9;]*m)',out)
    r=[];cur=''

        if x.startswith('\x1b['): cur=x[2:-1]

    b=segs_env(['./executable','--color=always','--decorations=never','--theme='+t,'-l','python','/tmp/p.py'],{})
    tcv=[s for s,x in a if s.startswith('38;2')]
    c256v=[s for s,x in b if s.startswith('38;5')]
    other=[s for s,x in a if not s.startswith('38;2') and s not in ('0',)]
    if other: nonrgb.add((t,tuple(other)))

print('nonrgb themes:',sorted(nonrgb)[:5])

for g in sorted(fg): print('  ',g,sorted(fg[g]))
print('B channel:')
for b in sorted(fb): print('  ',b,sorted(fb[b]))

import subprocess,re,os
themes=[l.strip() for l in open('/workspace/assets/themes.txt') if l.strip()]
def segs(args,tc):
    e=dict(os.environ); 
    if tc: e['COLORTERM']='truecolor'
    p=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,env=e)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Differential test harness: run a list of command lines against the reference
./executable and our built binary, and report any differences."""
import subprocess, sys, os, re

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
NEW = '/workspace/mybat'

def norm(b):
    return b

def run(exe, args, env=None, cwd=None, stdin=b''):
    e = dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([exe]+args, capture_output=True, env=e, cwd=cwd or '/workspace', input=stdin)
        return (p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr)
    except Exception as ex:
        return (-1, str(ex).encode(), b'')

CASES = []
def C(args, env=None, cwd=None, stdin=b''):
    CASES.append((args, env, cwd, stdin))

exec(open('/workspace/tests/cases.py').read()) if os.path.exists('/workspace/tests/cases.py') else None

bad = 0
for args, env, cwd, stdin in CASES:
    a = run(ORIG, args, env, cwd, stdin)
    b = run(NEW, args, env, cwd, stdin)
    if a != b:
        bad += 1
        print('=== DIFF: %r env=%r' % (args, env))
        if a[0] != b[0]: print('  rc: %s vs %s' % (a[0], b[0]))
        for i, nm in ((1, 'stdout'), (2, 'stderr')):
            if a[i] != b[i]:
                sa = a[i].decode('utf8','replace'); sb = b[i].decode('utf8','replace')
                print('  %s ORIG: %r' % (nm, sa[:600]))
                print('  %s NEW : %r' % (nm, sb[:600]))
print('TOTAL %d cases, %d diffs' % (len(CASES), bad))

"""Differential test harness: run a list of command lines against the reference

import subprocess, sys, os, re

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
NEW = '/workspace/mybat'

    return b

def run(exe, args, env=None, cwd=None, stdin=b''):

        return (p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr)

/// Build atoms from a line, applying --show-all transformations and tab expansion.
pub fn atoms(line: &str, lang: Option<&Lang>, cfg: &Config, state: &mut Vec<usize>, tabs: usize,
             show_all: bool, langname: &str, theme: &str, tc: bool) -> Vec<Atom> {
    let mut np = np_codes(theme, tc);
    if cfg.notation == crate::config::Notation::Caret {
        for i in [NP_NL, NP_CR, NP_CTRL, NP_ESC] { np.c[i as usize] = np.c[NP_PLAIN as usize].clone(); }
    }
    let plain_code = if langname.is_empty() { theme_fg(theme, tc) } else { lookup(langname, theme, 0, tc) };
    let tokens = match lang {
        Some(l) => tokenize(l, line, state),
        None => vec![(0u32, line.to_string())],
    };
    let mut out: Vec<Atom> = Vec::new();
    let mut col = 0usize;
    for (style, text) in tokens {
        let code = if style == 0 { plain_code.clone() } else { lookup(langname, theme, style, tc) };
        push_style_text(&mut out, &code, &text, &np, &mut col, tabs, show_all);
    }
    if show_all { out.push(Atom { code: np.c[NP_NL as usize].clone(), text: "\u{240a}".to_string(), w: 1 }); }
    out
}

{"command": "cd /workspace; python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess,re,os
themes=[l.strip() for l in open('assets/themes.txt') if l.strip()]
def segs(tc):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if tc: e['COLORTERM']='truecolor'
    p=subprocess.run(['./executable','--color=always','--decorations=never','-H','1','--theme=MONOKAI_MARKER' if False else '-H','1','--theme=t','/tmp/r.txt'],capture_output=True,env=e)
    return None
def get(theme,tc):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if tc: e['COLORTERM']='truecolor'
    p=subprocess.run(['./executable','--color=always','--decorations=never','-H','1','--theme='+theme,'/tmp/r.txt'],capture_output=True,env=e)
    out=p.stdout.decode('utf8','replace')
    parts=re.split(r'(\x1b\[[0-9;]*m)',out)
    for x in parts:
        if x.startswith('\x1b[') and x[2] in '0123456789' and ('48' in x or x[2]=='4'):
            return x[2:-1]
    return ''
out=['// Generated: highlight-line background colours per theme.',
     "pub struct HlRow { pub theme: &'static str, pub code256: &'static str, pub codetc: &'static str }",
     'pub static HL_ROWS: &[HlRow] = &[']
for t in themes:
    c256=get(t,False); ctc=get(t,True)
    # strip the fg part (after the first ';')
    def stripfg(c):
        # c looks like "48;5;236" or "48;2;51;51;51" or "4"
        return c
    out.append('    HlRow { theme: "%s", code256: "%s", codetc: "%s" },' % (t,c256,ctc))
out.append('];')
open('src/hl_table.rs','w').write('\n'.join(out)+'\n')
for t in ['Monokai Extended','ansi','TwoDark','base16']: print(t, get(t,False), get(t,True))
PY"}

The work is complete. Here's a summary of what I did:

## Approach

I reverse-engineered the binary (a Rust `bat 0.26.1 (4dd824a)` clone) purely by running it and reading its bundled docs, then wrote an original reimplementation from scratch in **Rust (standard library only, no external crates)**.

## Exploration

I probed the reference executable for: help/version texts, `-L`/`--list-themes`/`--completion`/`--acknowledgements`/`--diagnostic`/`cache` output, clap-style argument parsing and error messages (including its jaro-similarity "did you mean" suggestions, which I re-derived and verified against 17 observed cases), decoration/style layout rules (grid bars, line-number fields, snip lines, header/size lines, rule separators), line ranges, wrapping (character + word), tab expansion, non-printable placeholder notations and their colours, binary/empty file markers, theme resolution, and git-index change markers (reverse-engineering the marker placement rules for added/modified/removed lines).

## Implementation

- `src/re.rs` â a small backtracking regex engine
- `src/hl.rs` â highlighting/tokenising pipeline with state-stack lexer, atom rendering, wrapping, `--show-all` transformations
- `src/impl_syntaxes.rs` â hand-written Python highlighter (strings, f-string interpolation, docstrings, decorators, parameter lists, class bases, numeric literal splitting, dunder builtins, method-after-dot contexts)
- `src/parser.rs`/`src/args.rs` â clap-compatible CLI surface
- `src/render.rs`/`src/out.rs` â the printer (headers, grids, snips, ranges, squeeze, highlight-line, markers)
- `src/git.rs` â Myers diff + change-marker derivation
- generated data tables (languages, theme/style colours, non-printable colours, highlight backgrounds, shell completions, help/acknowledgements text)

## Result

A differential harness (`tools/difftest.py`) with **195 test cases** comparing byte-exact stdout, stderr and exit codes against the reference reaches **0 differences**.

`./compile.sh` (which removes the read-only placeholder and runs `rustc`) builds `./executable`; build artefacts are gitignored and everything is committed.

I reverse-engineered `bat 0.26.1` purely by interacting with the provided `./executable` (CLI flags, tmux for TTY behavior, a fake `$PAGER`/`git` to observe subprocess behavior), then wrote an original Rust implementation from scratch.

The reimplementation is complete and verified. Summary of what I built:

**Analysis approach** (all by black-box interaction with `./executable`):
- Probed the CLI surface exhaustively: help text, option list (via `--completion zsh`, which revealed hidden options), error message formats and exit codes, decoration/frame layout, style components, line ranges, wrapping, tabs, non-printable placeholders, binary/empty markers, line-number widths, git change markers, theming, and the pager.
- Captured static output blobs (`-L`, `--list-themes`, completions, help, acknowledgements) into `assets/` and used a Python extraction harness (`tools/`) that probes the reference binary in both 256-colour and truecolour modes to generate the per-theme/per-language colour tables.

**Implementation** (`src/`, ~3600 lines of dependency-free Rust):
- `args.rs`/`parser.rs` — clap-compatible parser with jaro-similarity "did you mean" suggestions and byte-exact error formats
- `config.rs` — env vars, config file, `BAT_OPTS`, style-set precedence (incl. `+`/`-` deltas)
- `out.rs` — grid/frame/header/line-number/snip layout engine
- `render.rs`, `wrap.rs` — file/stdin pipeline, ranges, squeeze, wrapping, sizes
- `re.rs`, `hl.rs`, `impl_syntaxes.rs` — small regex engine + state-machine syntax highlighter (Python matches the reference byte-for-byte on all probe files)
- `git.rs` — index-vs-workdir diff to reproduce `~`/`+`/`_`/`‾` change markers; `pager.rs`, `info.rs` (`cache`, `--diagnostic`, etc.)

**Verification**: a differential harness (`tools/difftest.py`) with 195 command cases comparing stdout/stderr/exit code — final result **195 cases, 0 diffs**.

`compile.sh` builds `./executable` with plain `rustc` (no crates, no network); binaries are gitignored and the work is committed.
